title: Continuous linear retraction onto a finite subextension of the normed algebraic closure
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extended absolute value, and finite intermediate fields $\mathbf Q_\ell\subseteq E\subseteq F\subseteq\Omega$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. There exists a continuous $E$-linear map
$$p_F:\Omega\longrightarrow F,\qquad p_F(a)=a\quad(a\in F),$$
where all fields have their norm topologies. Only linearity and continuity are required: $p_F$ need not be multiplicative, Galois-equivariant, or have operator norm at most one. No completeness of $\Omega$ is assumed.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent arithmetic expansion: continuous linear retraction used to detect a finite-field cocycle boundary. WANTED: nonarchimedean Hahn-Banach over the spherically complete local field E; no real/complex Hahn-Banach theorem is invoked.

proof.text: The induced norm on E is compatible with the given normed Q_l-algebra structure. It is nontrivial because Q_l is nontrivially normed [def-weil-l-adic-numbers], by Mathlib's intermediate-field nontrivially normed field instance. Since E is finite-dimensional over the complete proper field Q_l, FiniteDimensional.complete and FiniteDimensional.proper give completeness [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-complete] and properness [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-proper] for this actual induced norm. IsUltrametricDist.of_normedAlgebra transfers ultrametricity directly from Q_l to both E and Omega. Define the normed E-algebra structure on Omega using norm multiplicativity and the induced norm on E. No algebraic-closure exhaustion or uniqueness-of-absolute-value argument is needed.

source.place: Paragraph (3), coefficient-topology expansion: check the scalar and ambient hypotheses Agent expansion; not a proof supplied by the blueprint.

proof.text: Module.Finite.of_restrictScalars_finite gives finite-dimensionality of F over E from finite-dimensionality over Q_l and the canonical scalar tower. Let W be the E-submodule of Omega underlying F; the carriers, scalar actions and induced topologies of W and F agree definitionally. Choose the finite basis b=Module.finBasis E F. For every index i, turn b.coord i into f_i:W to E as a continuous E-linear map by LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap, using [lem-sfb-finite-dimensional-linear-map-continuous] and completeness and nontriviality of E from step 1.

source.place: Paragraph (3), coefficient-topology expansion: continuous finite-field coordinates Agent expansion; not a proof supplied by the blueprint.

proof.text: For each basis index, apply [lem-sfb-proper-ultrametric-scalar-extension] with K=E, V=Omega, W the submodule from step 2 and f=f_i. Step 1 supplies the normed-space, ultrametric and proper-space hypotheses, and NormedField.exists_norm_lt_one E supplies the nontrivial scalar. Choose g_i:Omega to E continuous and E-linear with g_i(w)=f_i(w) on W. Neither this step nor the cited extension theorem requires completeness of Omega.

source.place: Paragraph (3), coefficient-topology expansion: nonarchimedean scalar-functional extension Agent expansion; not a proof supplied by the blueprint.

proof.text: Set p to the finite sum of ContinuousLinearMap.smulRight (g_i) (b_i). This is a continuous E-linear map Omega to F by construction. For a in F, sum_apply and smulRight_apply express p(a) as the sum of g_i(a) times b_i. The extension identities replace each g_i(a) by (b.coord i)(a), and Basis.sum_repr identifies the result with a. This proves the unchanged retraction statement.

Step 1: uniqueness of the extended absolute value gives |.|_E; t=ell has |t|=ell^-1; closed balls are compact by properness, including radius r=0; Omega is ultrametric because x and y lie in a common finite L. Step 2: F/E is finite; the coordinate maps are continuous via LinearMap.continuous_of_finiteDimensional, and the topology on F is the subspace topology from Omega. Step 3: the hypotheses of the new node match exactly; neither node assumes completeness. Step 4 is an elementary assembly with p_F|F=id. Edge case F=E checked. The normalised-trace alternative is not continuous on Omega because |1/[L:F]| is unbounded, so the Hahn-Banach input is genuinely needed. The new node is Ingleton's non-archimedean Hahn-Banach theorem: compact closed balls imply spherical completeness, and I re-derived the Zorn plus nested-ball argument. It is true as stated without closedness of W or completeness of V, carries a statement only, introduces its own objects, and is a general lemma rather than a restatement of the item.
